event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: AVY’s 2022 Form 10-K describes COVID-19 as a still-unfolding, multifaceted threat that has already produced tangible harm (plant closures, $500 million emergency borrowing, negative 2020 results) and continues to cloud near-term outlooks.  The language is recent (within two years of filing) and mixes backward-looking impacts with forward-looking uncertainties about supply-chain reliability, labour availability, liquidity, and demand.  Although management highlights some mitigants (price increases, scenario planning, debt repayment), most statements emphasise unresolved risk and use strong material-adverse terminology.  Given the Time Decay Principle, evidence dated 2020-2022 qualifies for high—though not necessarily maximal—scores because the pandemic is ongoing and its future trajectory remains uncertain.  I therefore weight direct, quantified or operationally specific disclosures highest (scores 6-7) and assign moderate scores (3-5) to broader, more qualified or partially mitigated statements.

evidence_list.snippet: COVID-19 had an adverse effect on portions of our business and we could experience further negative consequences as a result of COVID-19 that could have a material adverse effect on our business.

components.reason: Direct admission of past adverse impact on business performance.
Explicit warning of additional future negative consequences.
Uses strong 'material adverse effect' language signalling severity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Past harm plus explicit future threat and severe wording merit a high recent-event score of 6.

evidence_list.snippet: We are unable to predict the full impact that COVID-19 will have on our business in 2022 due to numerous uncertainties, including the duration and severity of the pandemic, the impact of the spread of new and existing variants of the virus, the availability, adoption and effectiveness of vaccines and treatments, and containment measures and the related macroeconomic impacts.

components.reason: Highlights inability to forecast impact, underscoring uncertainty.
Enumerates multiple volatile drivers (variants, vaccines, containment).
Timeframe is immediate (2022), increasing relevance.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific near-term uncertainties raise risk to a solid 5 despite lack of quantification.

evidence_list.snippet: Delays in production or delivery of components or raw materials in our global supply chain, or the cost and ability to transport those components or materials or our finished goods, due to restrictions imposed to limit the spread of COVID-19 have delayed and could further delay or inhibit our ability to obtain supply of components and materials to deliver finished goods to customers, with these impacts and the higher cost of freight also increasing our costs.

components.reason: Reports actual supply-chain delays already experienced.
Warns of continued or worsening delays affecting ability to serve customers.
Notes cost inflation from freight, indicating financial impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Concrete operational disruptions plus forward-looking cost pressure justify a high risk score of 6.

evidence_list.snippet: In the first quarter of 2020, our ability to access the commercial paper market was disrupted as a result of the pandemic and we drew down $500 million from our revolving credit facility, which we repaid in the second quarter of 2020.

components.reason: Quantified emergency liquidity action ($500 million draw).
Directly links the liquidity stress to the pandemic.
Repayment shows partial mitigation.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Large, quantified cash draw underscores severity (score 6) but is slightly tempered by subsequent repayment.

evidence_list.snippet: If commercial paper markets or our ability to draw under our $800 million revolving credit facility were to become disrupted in the future due to the impact of COVID-19 on our customers, suppliers, vendors, and other business partners, our liquidity could be impacted which could materially adversely affect our business.

components.reason: Flags potential future liquidity crunch tied to pandemic conditions.
Mentions specific financing line ($800 million), adding concreteness.
Uses 'materially adversely affect' to convey magnitude.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking liquidity risk with quantified facility supports a moderate-high score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: Our office and management personnel in certain countries have generally worked from home since March 2020, and some of our employees engaged in manufacturing, production and distribution facilities have been at times restricted by governmental orders from coming to work.

components.reason: Indicates sustained remote-work shift for office staff.
Governmental restrictions limiting on-site production labour.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Operational/labour disruptions are significant but not quantified, resulting in a score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: The pandemic has already constrained the labor market, with certain individuals electing to leave their current positions or the workforce entirely (commonly referred to as the “great resignation”) and both prospective and current employees more actively seeking higher compensation and benefits in what has become known as the “war for talent.”

components.reason: Describes labour shortages directly traceable to pandemic ('great resignation').
Highlights cost pressure from higher wage expectations.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Labour scarcity and cost inflation elevate risk to 4.

evidence_list.snippet: Macroeconomic developments such as impacts from COVID-19, inflation, raw material, freight and labor availability, slower growth in the geographic regions in which we operate and uncertainty in the global credit or financial markets leading to a loss of consumer confidence could result in a material adverse effect on our business as a result of, among other things, reduced consumer spending, declines in asset valuations, diminished liquidity and credit availability, volatility in securities prices, credit rating downgrades and fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates.

components.reason: Lists COVID-19 among macro factors capable of causing material harm.
Provides detailed cascade of potential financial impacts.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Broad, somewhat generic macro-level warning scores a moderate 3.

evidence_list.snippet: In early 2020, in response to the initial outbreak of COVID-19, many of our manufacturing and other operations in China experienced limited production and/or closure; as the outbreak spread beyond this region, our facilities in other countries were similarly impacted, most significantly in South Asia in late 2020.

components.reason: Details concrete plant shutdowns and limited production.
Specifies multiple geographies (China, South Asia), showing breadth.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific multi-region operational shutdowns earn a 4.

evidence_list.snippet: In 2021, with the spread of the Delta variant mid-year, we experienced intermittent closures in Southeast Asia, particularly in our RBIS reportable segment.

components.reason: Recent (2021) variant-driven facility closures.
Identifies affected business segment (RBIS).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Recency and segment specificity justify a score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: Overall, COVID-19 had a negative impact on our consolidated financial results in 2020, most significantly in our RBIS and IHM reportable segments; its direct impact on our operations in 2021 was more modest.

components.reason: Affirms negative financial impact in 2020.
Names specific segments harmed.
Notes improvement in 2021, which partially mitigates risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Past financial damage balanced by improving trend yields a net score of 3.

evidence_list.snippet: COVID-19 has adversely affected the economies and financial markets in virtually all countries, and further escalation of the pandemic could lead to a more significant economic downturn that could adversely affect demand for our products and negatively impact our business.

components.reason: Acknowledges broad global economic harm already occurring.
Warns of deeper downturn and demand destruction if pandemic worsens.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Global scope and forward-looking demand risk merit a 4.
